* Add Wikipedia download and extract stage

This commit introduces a comprehensive pipeline for downloading and processing Wikipedia dump files within the ray-curator framework. Key components include:

- **WikipediaUrlGenerator**: Generates URLs for Wikipedia dump files.
- **WikipediaDownloader**: Downloads .bz2 dump files using wget.
- **WikipediaIterator**: Parses Wikipedia XML dumps and extracts article content.
- **WikipediaExtractor**: Cleans Wikipedia markup and extracts meaningful text.

Additionally, an example script demonstrating the usage of the new stage is included, along with tests for each component to ensure functionality and reliability.

Documentation for the new stage is also provided to guide users in implementation and usage.

This commit introduces a comprehensive pipeline for downloading and processing Wikipedia dump files within the ray-curator framework. Key components include:

- **WikipediaUrlGenerator**: Generates URLs for Wikipedia dump files.
- **WikipediaDownloader**: Downloads .bz2 dump files using wget.
- **WikipediaIterator**: Parses Wikipedia XML dumps and extracts article content.
- **WikipediaExtractor**: Cleans Wikipedia markup and extracts meaningful text.

Additionally, an example script demonstrating the usage of the new stage is included, along with tests for each component to ensure functionality and reliability.

Documentation for the new stage is also provided to guide users in implementation and usage.

- **WikipediaUrlGenerator**: Generates URLs for Wikipedia dump files.

- **WikipediaExtractor**: Cleans Wikipedia markup and extracts meaningful text.

Additionally, an example script demonstrating the usage of the new stage is included, along with tests for each component to ensure functionality and reliability.

Documentation for the new stage is also provided to guide users in implementation and usage.

* Add Wikipedia download and extract stage

This commit introduces a comprehensive pipeline for downloading and processing Wikipedia dump files within the ray-curator framework. Key components include:

- **WikipediaUrlGenerator**: Generates URLs for Wikipedia dump files.
- **WikipediaDownloader**: Downloads .bz2 dump files using wget.
- **WikipediaIterator**: Parses Wikipedia XML dumps and extracts article content.
- **WikipediaExtractor**: Cleans Wikipedia markup and extracts meaningful text.

Additionally, an example script demonstrating the usage of the new stage is included, along with tests for each component to ensure functionality and reliability.

Documentation for the new stage is also provided to guide users in implementation and usage.

* Add Wikipedia download and extract stage

This commit introduces a comprehensive pipeline for downloading and processing Wikipedia dump files within the ray-curator framework. Key components include:

- **WikipediaUrlGenerator**: Generates URLs for Wikipedia dump files.
- **WikipediaDownloader**: Downloads .bz2 dump files using wget.
- **WikipediaIterator**: Parses Wikipedia XML dumps and extracts article content.
- **WikipediaExtractor**: Cleans Wikipedia markup and extracts meaningful text.

Additionally, an example script demonstrating the usage of the new stage is included, along with tests for each component to ensure functionality and reliability.

Documentation for the new stage is also provided to guide users in implementation and usage.

* Add Wikipedia download and extract stage

This commit introduces a comprehensive pipeline for downloading and processing Wikipedia dump files within the ray-curator framework. Key components include:

- **WikipediaUrlGenerator**: Generates URLs for Wikipedia dump files.
- **WikipediaDownloader**: Downloads .bz2 dump files using wget.
- **WikipediaIterator**: Parses Wikipedia XML dumps and extracts article content.
- **WikipediaExtractor**: Cleans Wikipedia markup and extracts meaningful text.

Additionally, an example script demonstrating the usage of the new stage is included, along with tests for each component to ensure functionality and reliability.

Documentation for the new stage is also provided to guide users in implementation and usage.

* Add Wikipedia download and extract stage

This commit introduces a comprehensive pipeline for downloading and processing Wikipedia dump files within the ray-curator framework. Key components include:

- **WikipediaUrlGenerator**: Generates URLs for Wikipedia dump files.
- **WikipediaDownloader**: Downloads .bz2 dump files using wget.
- **WikipediaIterator**: Parses Wikipedia XML dumps and extracts article content.
- **WikipediaExtractor**: Cleans Wikipedia markup and extracts meaningful text.

Additionally, an example script demonstrating the usage of the new stage is included, along with tests for each component to ensure functionality and reliability.

Documentation for the new stage is also provided to guide users in implementation and usage.

new extension: rich metadata for SEO (#1182)

* docs(extensions): add rich metadata SEO extension with frontmatter integration

Add new Sphinx extension that injects SEO-optimized metadata into HTML head from frontmatter:

Core Features:
- Extract frontmatter (description, tags, personas, difficulty, content_type, modality)
- Generate standard meta tags (description, keywords, audience)
- Generate Open Graph tags for social sharing (Facebook, LinkedIn)
- Generate Twitter Card tags for enhanced previews
- Generate JSON-LD structured data (schema.org) for search engines
- Support product versioning via cascade.product fields

Components:
- rich_metadata/__init__.py: Main extension with config-inited and html-page-context hooks
- rich_metadata/templates/layout.html: Template override for metadata injection
- rich_metadata/README.md: Technical overview and features
- rich_metadata/USAGE.md: Complete usage guide with examples
- rich_metadata/SUMMARY.md: Quick reference guide
- rich_metadata/IMPLEMENTATION.md: Architecture and implementation details
- rich_metadata/verify_metadata.py: Automated verification script

Template handling follows search_assets pattern - templates live within extension folder
and are automatically added to Sphinx template search path via config-inited hook.

Extension enabled in conf.py and ready for use with existing frontmatter.

* Add Common Crawl raw content fetching stage

This commit implements the high-fidelity data extraction pipeline described in the Nemotron-CC-Math paper. It adds the ability to reprocess math datasets by fetching the original raw HTML content directly from Common Crawl snapshots, rather than relying on pre-extracted text.

Key Changes:
- Added `CommonCrawlWARCReader` stage: Fetches raw WARC records from the public Common Crawl S3 bucket using byte-range requests.

subject: Add ALM Data Pipeline tutorial and stages (#1419)
message:
Add ALM Data Pipeline tutorial and stages (#1419)

* feat: Add ALM Data Pipeline tutorial and stages

Add new NeMo Curator stages for ALM (Audio Language Model) data curation:
- ALMDataBuilderStage: Creates training windows from audio segments with
  quality filtering (sample rate, bandwidth, speaker count, duration)
- ALMDataOverlapStage: Filters overlapping windows based on threshold,
  keeping windows closest to target duration

Add complete tutorial with:
- YAML-driven pipeline configuration (main.py + pipeline.yaml)
- Sample input data for testing
- Comprehensive documentation with pipeline flow diagram

Add unit tests for both stages (14 tests, all passing).

The output JSONL is consumed by downstream processors, producing
sharded data ready for training Audio Language Models.

Tested with sample data:
- Stage 1 produces 181 windows from 5 input entries
- Stage 2 filters to 25 non-overlapping windows (3035.5s total)

subject: feat(interleaved): Foundation IO improvements — schema utilities, base-class fixes, and bug fixes (#1652)
message:
feat(interleaved): Foundation IO improvements — schema utilities, base-class fixes, and bug fixes (#1652)

* feat(interleaved): foundation IO improvements — schema utilities, base-class fixes, and bug fixes

Splits out the foundation layer from PR #1570 as a standalone PR:

Schema utilities (utils/schema.py — new):
- reconcile_schema(): canonical types for reserved columns, passthrough columns preserved
- align_table(): pad, reorder, cast tables to a target schema; safe=True for passthrough
  columns to surface overflow errors instead of silently corrupting data (B5 fix)

Reader base (readers/base.py):
- Add schema= and schema_overrides= parameters for strict schema alignment
- _resolve_schema() helper: schema > schema_overrides > INTERLEAVED_SCHEMA priority
- Warn (not silently ignore) when both schema= and schema_overrides= are provided (C5)
- Fix return type annotation: -> pa.Schema | None (C4)
- Preserve nullable=False from INTERLEAVED_SCHEMA when applying schema_overrides (C6)

Writer base (writers/base.py):
- Add schema= and schema_overrides= for output alignment (same API as reader)
- Add on_materialize_error= parameter: "error"|"warn"|"drop_row"|"drop_sample"
- _materialize_dataframe(): apply error policy after fetch; guard binary_content column
- Make _write_dataframe() non-abstract (default pass body) to allow WDS-style overrides (D3)

Materialization (utils/materialization.py):
- _build_global_range_index(): group paths by filesystem object so mixed-backend batches
  work correctly (B3 fix)

WebDataset reader (readers/webdataset.py):
- Rename tiff result variable to tiff_frame to remove variable shadowing (D5 fix)

Parquet reader (readers/parquet.py):
- Guard pq.read_schema() call behind if self.fields is not None to avoid N+1 schema
  reads in the common case (C1 fix)

Tests:
- test_base_writer.py (new): 9 tests covering on_materialize_error modes, schema
  alignment, and write_data orchestration
- test_materialization.py: 4 new tests for multi-backend path grouping (B3)
- test_multimodal_core.py: 4 new align_table tests for safe-cast behaviour (B5)
- test_multimodal_reader.py: schema_overrides and nullable preservation tests (C5/C6)
- conftest.py: additional helpers for new test patterns

Note: InterleavedParquetReader, InterleavedParquetReaderStage, and
InterleavedWebdatasetWriterStage are intentionally excluded from this branch;
they will be added in the follow-up PR on feat/interleaved-io-readers-writers.

Signed-off-by: u5a826e42969b1d4a <u5a826e42969b1d4a@users.invalid>

  defined in readers/base.py and imported by writers/base.py)
- Renamed _resolve_schema to resolve_schema (public shared utility)
- Returns None when both args are None instead of unreachable ValueError

writers/base.py:

  forces index=False) so write_data() no longer copies the dict on every task

* feat(interleaved): foundation IO improvements — schema utilities, base-class fixes, and bug fixes

Splits out the foundation layer from PR #1570 as a standalone PR:

Schema utilities (utils/schema.py — new):
- reconcile_schema(): canonical types for reserved columns, passthrough columns preserved
- align_table(): pad, reorder, cast tables to a target schema; safe=True for passthrough
  columns to surface overflow errors instead of silently corrupting data (B5 fix)

Reader base (readers/base.py):
- Add schema= and schema_overrides= parameters for strict schema alignment
- _resolve_schema() helper: schema > schema_overrides > INTERLEAVED_SCHEMA priority
- Warn (not silently ignore) when both schema= and schema_overrides= are provided (C5)
- Fix return type annotation: -> pa.Schema | None (C4)
- Preserve nullable=False from INTERLEAVED_SCHEMA when applying schema_overrides (C6)

Writer base (writers/base.py):
- Add schema= and schema_overrides= for output alignment (same API as reader)
- Add on_materialize_error= parameter: "error"|"warn"|"drop_row"|"drop_sample"
- _materialize_dataframe(): apply error policy after fetch; guard binary_content column
- Make _write_dataframe() non-abstract (default pass body) to allow WDS-style overrides (D3)

Materialization (utils/materialization.py):
- _build_global_range_index(): group paths by filesystem object so mixed-backend batches
  work correctly (B3 fix)

WebDataset reader (readers/webdataset.py):
- Rename tiff result variable to tiff_frame to remove variable shadowing (D5 fix)

Parquet reader (readers/parquet.py):
- Guard pq.read_schema() call behind if self.fields is not None to avoid N+1 schema

- test_base_writer.py (new): 9 tests covering on_materialize_error modes, schema
  alignment, and write_data orchestration

subject: [benchmarking] updates SlackSink and process logging to support parallel benchmark runs (#1678)
message:
[benchmarking] updates SlackSink and process logging to support parallel benchmark runs (#1678)

* benchmarking: update SlackSink to support parallel benchmark runs

Uses a shared JSON state file (.slack_state.json) in the session
directory to coordinate between concurrent SlackSink instances. One
instance wins an atomic O_CREAT|O_EXCL race to become the session
owner, posts the parent Slack message, and writes the initial state.
Followers poll the state file for the parent message timestamp and
reconstruct their local parent message from it.

Parent message updates use fcntl.LOCK_EX to serialize the
read-modify-write cycle and Slack API call across processes, ensuring
no instance overwrites another's entry status with stale data.

Also removes _finalize_session_summary_message(), which marked
unfinished entries as errors — not meaningful in a parallel context
where different processes own different entries.

Add Nemotron-Parse PDF processing pipeline (#1693)

* Add Nemotron-Parse PDF processing stages and benchmarking script

This commit introduces a comprehensive set of stages for processing PDFs using the Nemotron-Parse pipeline, including partitioning, preprocessing, inference, postprocessing, and utility functions. A new benchmarking script is also added to evaluate the performance of the pipeline, collecting detailed metrics during execution.

Key additions:
- New stages: PDFPartitioningStage, PDFPreprocessStage, NemotronParseInferenceStage, NemotronParsePostprocessStage, and utility functions for rendering and output parsing.
- Benchmarking script for performance evaluation and metrics collection.
- Tests for the new stages to ensure functionality and correctness.

These enhancements aim to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of PDF processing within the framework.

Signed-off-by: u46dbc2cd55a95df4 <u46dbc2cd55a95df4@users.invalid>

* Add PDF parsing configuration fields and update main pipeline

This commit introduces new configuration fields for handling PDF filenames and source URLs in the NemotronParsePDFReader class. The changes include:

- Added `file_name_field`, `file_names_field`, and `url_field` attributes to specify JSONL field names for single and multiple PDF filenames, as well as the source URL.
- Updated the argument parser in the main script to accept these new fields, enhancing the flexibility of the PDF processing pipeline.
- Integrated a RayClient for improved resource management during pipeline execution.

These enhancements aim to streamline the PDF processing workflow and improve user configurability.

Signed-off-by: u46dbc2cd55a95df4 <u46dbc2cd55a95df4@users.invalid>

subject: Add SlurmRayClient for multi-node Ray cluster management on SLURM (#1712)
message:
Add SlurmRayClient for multi-node Ray cluster management on SLURM (#1712)

* Add SlurmRayClient for multi-node Ray cluster management on SLURM

SlurmRayClient extends RayClient to handle the multi-process SLURM
job model where srun launches one Python process per node.

Key design:
- Node 0 (SLURM_NODEID=0) starts the Ray head via `ray start --head`
  and writes the GCS port to a shared file (RAY_PORT_BROADCAST_DIR or
  /tmp) so all other nodes can discover it
- Nodes 1+ wait for the port file, then run `ray start --block
  --address=<head>:<port>` as workers; start() returns immediately on
  worker nodes so user code only runs on the head
- Head waits for all allocated nodes to appear in `ray.nodes()` before
  returning (configurable via worker_connect_timeout_s)
- Graceful teardown: head calls `ray stop` and removes the port file;
  workers exit naturally once the head stops
- Port collision avoidance with _pick_free_port() using socket SO_REUSEADDR
- SIGALRM-based timeout on ray.init() to detect hung GCS connections

Parameters:
- ray_port: GCS port (default: random free port)
- ray_temp_dir: shared temp dir for Ray logs/sockets
- num_gpus / num_cpus: resource overrides passed to `ray start`
- worker_connect_timeout_s: how long to wait for all nodes to join
- gpu_enforcement_interval_s: if >0, periodically checks GPU count
  matches expected and raises if enforcement fails

subject: Fix waveform tensor leak in audio pipeline and redesign AudioDataFilterStage for all VAD/Speaker combinations (#1765)
message:
Fix waveform tensor leak in audio pipeline and redesign AudioDataFilterStage for all VAD/Speaker combinations (#1765)

* Fix waveform tensor leak and redesign AudioDataFilterStage for all VAD/Speaker combos

Fixes the OverflowError crash in JsonlWriter caused by torch.Tensor
waveform leaking through the pipeline into serialization.

Root cause: When VAD and SpeakerSeparation were disabled, no cleanup
stage ran before AudioToDocumentStage, so MonoConversionStage's
waveform tensor leaked into the DataFrame and crashed ujson.

Changes:

- Redesign AudioDataFilterStage.decompose() as a topology selector
  with 4 distinct pipeline builders (one per VAD/Speaker combo),
  each producing a self-consistent stage sequence ending with
  TimestampMapper.

- Separate VAD (_make_vad) from quality filters (_append_quality_filters)
  for clarity: VAD is a segmentation stage, not a filter.

- Fix TimestampMapper to handle all 4 combos:
  1. segment_mappings (full pipeline with SegmentConcat)
  2. start_ms/end_ms (VAD fan-out)
  3. diar_segments (SpeakerSep with speaker timing)
  4. duration fallback (filters only, whole file)

- Replace confusing _STRIP_KEYS blacklist with clean two-layer output
  control: _NEVER_PASS_KEYS safety net (blocks tensors always) +
  passthrough_keys whitelist (user-configurable, sensible default).

- Fix SpeakerSeparation to propagate diar_segments from diarization
  model so Combo 3 output has meaningful speaker timing data.

- Standardize duration key to "duration" across all stages.

- Add BandFilter warning on unexpected prediction values.

- Update extract_segments.py to handle all 4 combos with auto-detection,
  metadata.csv generation, and generic score extraction.

- Add --execution-mode flag to pipeline.py for batch/streaming control.

- Update README.md and pipeline.yaml with topology documentation.

* Address PR review: fix unreachable combo detection, clarify core vs passthrough fields

- Remove unreachable extract_combo1 (TimestampMapper always sets timestamps)
- Merge combos 1 & 2 into extract_segments_by_timestamps
- Rename extraction functions to be descriptive
- Document diar_segments/speaking_duration as core fields in TimestampMapper docstring

* Fix test_decompose_all_disabled_except_mono to expect TimestampMapperStage

TimestampMapperStage is the pipeline output normalizer and must always
be present. Updated test assertion from 1 to 2 stages and added type
check for TimestampMapperStage.

* Add non-serializable key sanitization and refactor extract_segments

- AudioToDocumentStage: strip torch tensors and known non-serializable
  keys (waveform, audio, segments, etc.) before DataFrame construction
  as a safety net for upstream stages that miss cleanup.
- TimestampMapper: add warning log when no timing info is found and a
  zero-duration row is emitted.
- Add unit tests for _translate_to_original covering exact match,
  partial overlap, cross-boundary, silence gaps, and malformed mappings.
- Refactor extract_segments.py: deduplicate combo extraction functions
  into a shared _extract_file_segments engine with combo-specific
  callables for intervals, filenames, and metadata.
- Fix README Combo 1 description to match actual output naming.

* Fix ruff lint errors in test_timestamp_mapper and extract_segments

* Address PR review: SpeakerResult NamedTuple, docs, passthrough_keys

- Replace fragile tuple return type in get_speaker_audio_data with
  SpeakerResult NamedTuple for self-documenting named field access.
- Update caller in speaker_separation.py to use result.audio,
  result.duration, result.diar_segments instead of positional unpacking.
- Document _INHERITED_DROP_KEYS explaining why duration/num_samples
  are dropped from parent tasks during speaker separation.
- Add comments in pipeline.py and pipeline.yaml documenting the
  default passthrough_keys and how to restrict output columns.
- Add speaker separation note to README explaining dropped keys.

* Fix test mocks to use SpeakerResult NamedTuple

Update test_speaker_separation.py to construct SpeakerResult
instead of plain tuples, matching the named attribute access
introduced in speaker_separation.py.

* refactor: move extract_segments logic into SegmentExtractionStage

Move reusable segment extraction functions from the tutorial script
into the nemo_curator package as a proper ProcessingStage. The tutorial
becomes a thin CLI wrapper importing from the package.

- Add nemo_curator/stages/audio/io/extract_segments.py with
  SegmentExtractionStage (ProcessingStage[AudioTask, AudioTask])
- Slim tutorials/audio/readspeech/extract_segments.py to CLI wrapper
- Add tests/stages/audio/io/test_extract_segments.py with clean imports

* fix: accumulate metadata rows across batches in SegmentExtractionStage

* fix: persistent counters for all combos and single-worker constraint

* fix: NameError in run.py, lazy executor factory, reduce GPU allocations to fit single GPU

- launch_disagg_replicas + _launch_disagg_role: one detached PG per prefill
  and decode worker (single-bundle STRICT_PACK). Decode launched first
  (Dynamo example convention); only prefill publishes ZMQ KV events.
- resolve_disagg_role_config: merges role-level engine_kwargs over the
  model-wide engine_kwargs so callers override only what they need per role.
- plan_disagg_shape: rejects multi-node TP up front (disagg requires each
  role's TP group to fit on one node).
- Default kv_transfer_config = NixlConnector + kv_both; overridable via the
  init=False DynamoVLLMModelConfig.kv_transfer_config field.
- Per-worker VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT via get_free_port_in_bundle with a
  stable seed so concurrent workers on one node don't collide.

Cross-model validators (nemo_curator/core/serve/dynamo/backend.py)
- _validate_unique_model_names: rejects duplicate model_name and slug
  collisions (both would silently overwrite each other inside etcd under
  dyn://namespace.component.endpoint).
- _validate_gpu_requirements(topology=...): adds the disagg-role-fit-
  one-node check alongside the existing aggregate-capacity check.
- DynamoBackend.start() no longer raises NotImplementedError for
  mode='disagg'; dispatches to launch_disagg_replicas.

_validate_frontend_config from v2 is intentionally dropped. In the typed
API, namespace / request_plane / event_plane / router all live once on
DynamoServerConfig, so there is nothing to validate for coherence across
models.

Router polish
- _resolve_effective_router_mode: when the user leaves router.mode=None
  and any model is disagg, auto-pick 'kv' so the frontend consumes the
  KV events prefill workers publish.
- _launch_frontend emits --router-mode (when set) and
  --[no-]router-kv-events (only when mode='kv', driven off the typed
  DynamoRouterConfig.kv_events). Any other --router-* knob flows through
  router_kwargs via the existing snake-to-kebab engine_kwargs_to_cli_flags
  translator; no typed resolver layer.
- DynamoRouterConfig rejects router_mode / router_kv_events inside
  router_kwargs at __post_init__ (typed-field shadow guard).

Tests
- tests/core/serve/dynamo/test_vllm.py: disagg helpers + launch_disagg_
  replicas CLI coverage, using the shared captured_spawn fixture and the
  real plan_replica_bundle_shape against injected topology (house pattern
  from 3e90016b).
- tests/core/serve/dynamo/test_backend.py: validator + router-mode
  resolution + frontend router-kv-events/override tests.
- tests/core/serve/dynamo/test_config.py: reserved-router-kwargs
  rejection.
- tests/core/serve/integration/test_dynamo.py: end-to-end disagg GPU
  test (1 prefill + 1 decode, TP=1) exercising the real Dynamo
  frontend + etcd + NATS + Nixl KV transfer path.

Verified with ruff + pytest tests/core/serve/ -m "not gpu" (91 passed)
and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 pytest tests/core/serve/integration/
test_dynamo.py -m gpu (3/3 passed, 8m29s).

* fix(serve): always pass --kv-events-config on disagg decode workers

Mirror the aggregated path: build a KV-events config blob with
enabled=publishes_kv_events (True for prefill, False for decode) and
unconditionally emit --kv-events-config on every disagg worker.

Without this, decode workers fall back to Dynamo's args.py auto-creation
of a KVEventsConfig bound to tcp://*:20080 when vLLM prefix_caching is
enabled (>=0.16 default), causing every decode worker on the same node
to fight over that port. The 1+1 integration test only has one decode
worker, so the bug was not surfaced there but would trigger as soon as
num_decode_replicas > 1 or multi-model disagg placed two decode workers
on the same node.

Update the TestLaunchDisaggReplicas CLI-arg assertions so both prefill
(enabled=True) and decode (enabled=False, no endpoint) are locked in.

Flagged by greptile-apps on PR #1861.

Signed-off-by: u614bb9053f1f3f74 <u614bb9053f1f3f74@users.invalid>

* fix(serve): auto-enable router.kv_events when auto-picking mode="kv" for disagg

Previously ``_resolve_effective_router_mode`` auto-picked ``mode="kv"``
when the caller left ``router.mode=None`` and any model was disagg, but
``router.kv_events`` kept its ``False`` default. The frontend then
emitted ``--router-mode kv --no-router-kv-events`` while prefill workers
unconditionally publish KV events in disagg — the router silently fell
back to approximate tree-based tracking and ignored the events
publishers were generating.

Replace ``_resolve_effective_router_mode`` with ``_resolve_effective_router``
returning ``(mode, kv_events)``. When we auto-pick ``mode="kv"`` (i.e.
``router.mode=None`` + disagg model present) we also auto-enable
``kv_events=True`` so the publisher/consumer stay in sync. Users who
set ``router.mode`` explicitly — including ``mode="kv"`` with
``kv_events=False`` — retain full control.

Thread the resolved value through ``launch_replicas`` (so aggregated
workers publish events when the router expects them) and through
``_launch_frontend`` (new ``effective_router_kv_events`` parameter).

Rewrite ``TestResolveEffectiveRouter`` to lock in the combined
resolution (explicit/auto, kv/non-kv, disagg/aggregated). Update
``test_effective_router_overrides_are_honored`` so the auto-resolve
path asserts ``--router-kv-events``.

Flagged by greptile-apps on PR #1861.

Signed-off-by: u614bb9053f1f3f74 <u614bb9053f1f3f74@users.invalid>

* fix(serve): use global worker_index for disagg KV events port seed

Matches the NIXL port pattern on line 436. Previously per-role i caused
prefill + decode workers on the same node to share port seeds; currently
harmless since decode has enabled=False, but latent collision risk if
build_worker_kv_events_config ever allocates regardless of enabled.

Addresses PR 1861 review feedback.

* fix(serve): address PR 1861 review feedback

- Thread worker_index_offset through launch_disagg_replicas so the
  first worker of every disagg model doesn't share Nixl/KV-events
  port seeds. DynamoBackend now accumulates a cross-model counter.
  Addresses greptile P1: same-node placement of two disagg models
